claim: A material methodology change (new evidence-tier rule, population code or synthesis tier) triggers self-review against the section 2.2 risk vectors and an update of section 3.3 if elements are affected.

speaker: PROCESS_RULE
subject: review cadence on adversarial catalogue extension
claim: An adversarial-use catalogue extension touching legal or regulatory matter triggers same-session review of the section 3.3 provisional language.

speaker: PROCESS_RULE
subject: cross-stage coverage
claim: No additional cross-stage thread is required for the legal framework; CS9 adversarial-use review covers V-08 reviewability.

speaker: PROCESS_RULE
subject: architecture document content
claim: The architecture document must not log specific issues, decisions or session activity; that content lives in decisions/, audits/, sessions/ and git history.

speaker: RATIFIED_DOC
subject: repository convention
claim: The repository has a single primary author, a main branch protected by CI, and an authoritative data layer.

speaker: RATIFIED_DOC
subject: deployment surface
claim: The project's surface is claude.ai chat with Code Interpreter.

speaker: PROCESS_RULE
subject: runtime layer precedence
claim: Three runtime layers (user preferences, project instructions, skills/hooks/CI) govern behavior; the outer layer wins by default and layers override only via explicit named clauses.

speaker: PROCESS_RULE
subject: PI overriding preferences
claim: Project instructions override user preferences only via an explicit clause naming the rule and scope.

speaker: PROCESS_RULE
subject: skill versus PI precedence
claim: Skills override project instructions on mechanics while project instructions govern whether and when a skill runs.

speaker: PROCESS_RULE
subject: code-enforced checks versus text rules
claim: Code-enforced checks (hooks, CI) trump text rules for the matching invariant.

speaker: RATIFIED_DOC
subject: data layer
claim: A data layer of data/guidebook.db, schemas/ and scripts/migrations/ sits beneath all three runtime layers.

speaker: RATIFIED_DOC
subject: derived artifacts read from data layer
claim: The website and all derived artifacts must read from the data layer.

speaker: RATIFIED_DOC
subject: direct DB writes
claim: Direct writes to the database that bypass migrations are prohibited.

speaker: PROCESS_RULE
subject: reference file content
claim: Reference files hold rules, taxonomies and structured registries and must not hold session activity, dated reports or transient state.

speaker: PROCESS_RULE
subject: extraction of session content from reference files
claim: Session-specific notes, dated commentary and resolved-item logs in a reference file are extracted to the appropriate directory.

speaker: PROCESS_RULE
subject: reference file stability
claim: Reference files should read the same six months from now as today.

speaker: RATIFIED_DOC
subject: decisions directory
claim: decisions/ holds Decision Records named DR-YYYY-MM-DD-slug.md and transient deployment queues.

speaker: RATIFIED_DOC
subject: _archived directory
claim: _archived/ holds files removed from active circulation but preserved for git history.

speaker: RATIFIED_DOC
subject: decision register
claim: data/decisions/decision_register.yaml, mirrored into the decisions table, tracks granular in-session decisions with D-NNNN identifiers.

speaker: RATIFIED_DOC
subject: register decisions versus Decision Records
claim: Register decisions (D-NNNN) and Decision Records (DR-YYYY-MM-DD) are related but distinct and neither supersedes the other.

speaker: PROCESS_RULE
subject: PI skill assignments
claim: The PI declares skill assignments as one-line entries; detail lives in references/skill-registry.md.

speaker: RATIFIED_DOC
subject: skill file layout
claim: Skill files are flat at skills/<name>_SKILL.md and deprecated skills live in skills/deprecated/ and are not loaded on trigger.

speaker: PROCESS_RULE
subject: skill universality
claim: A skill file must not cite specific session IDs, dates, commit SHAs, gaps or an embedded changelog.

speaker: PROCESS_RULE
subject: skill project state location
claim: Project-specific state a skill operates on lives in the database or in DRs referenced by stable identifier, not in the skill.

speaker: PROCESS_RULE
subject: skill placeholder convention
claim: When PI references a skill with no file, it states "skill placeholder" or "no skill file exists" inline.

speaker: PROCESS_RULE
subject: drift between PI and skills
claim: Drift between PI references and skills/ content is reconciled in references/skill-registry.md, not in the PI.

speaker: PROCESS_RULE
subject: enforcement levels
claim: Rules live at one of five enforcement levels: text rule, audit script, non-blocking CI workflow, blocking CI workflow, pre-commit hook.

speaker: PROCESS_RULE
subject: enforcement level 2
claim: Enforcement level 2 is an audit script at scripts/audit/*.py run manually or on a schedule.

speaker: PROCESS_RULE
subject: enforcement level 4
claim: Enforcement level 4 is a blocking CI workflow in .github/workflows/*.yml with continue-on-error false.

speaker: PROCESS_RULE
subject: new rule enforcement start
claim: New rules start at enforcement level 1 as text in PI standing rules.

speaker: PROCESS_RULE
subject: promotion to level 2
claim: A rule that is mechanically checkable and whose drift is observably costly is promoted to level 2 by writing an audit script.

speaker: PROCESS_RULE
subject: promotion to level 4
claim: A rule that must never drift in main is promoted to level 4 by adding its audit script as a blocking CI job.

speaker: PROCESS_RULE
subject: pre-commit hooks
claim: Pre-commit hooks (level 5) are deferred until the contributor count exceeds one.

speaker: PROCESS_RULE
subject: audit script demotion
claim: Audit scripts that have found no issue in 6 months may be downgraded to scheduled execution rather than per-push.

speaker: PROCESS_RULE
subject: audit script docstring
claim: An audit script's module docstring lists its checks numerically with rule provenance.

speaker: PROCESS_RULE
subject: audit script exit codes
claim: An audit script exits 0 on pass and 1 on any issue found.

speaker: PROCESS_RULE
subject: audit script repository root
claim: An audit script resolves the repository root relative to __file__ with no hardcoded absolute paths.

speaker: PROCESS_RULE
subject: audit script DB path
claim: An audit script's DB path defaults to data/guidebook.db and is overridable via the GUIDEBOOK_DB_PATH environment variable.

speaker: RATIFIED_DOC
subject: database as single source of truth
claim: data/guidebook.db is the single source of truth for project content.

speaker: RATIFIED_DOC
subject: markdown and JSON competing with the database
claim: Markdown files and JSON exports may derive from the database but must never compete with it.

speaker: RATIFIED_DOC
subject: schema migrations
claim: Schema changes ship as forward-only numbered SQL migrations scripts/migrations/NNN_<slug>.sql tracked via PRAGMA user_version.

speaker: RATIFIED_DOC
subject: data migrations
claim: Data changes ship as forward-only, append-only timestamped migrations scripts/migrations/data_<YYYYMMDDHHMMSS>_<slug>.sql tracked via the data_migrations table.

speaker: RATIFIED_DOC
subject: migration runner
claim: scripts/migrate_db.py applies pending migrations on push and supports --rebuild for CI reproducibility verification.

speaker: RATIFIED_DOC
subject: reproducibility invariant
claim: The committed data/guidebook.db must be reproducible from its migration history.
enforcement: CI rebuilds a fresh DB by replaying all migrations and compares key invariants

speaker: RATIFIED_DOC
subject: Pydantic mirrors SQLite
claim: Pydantic schemas in schemas/ must mirror the SQLite layout; drift is a CI-detectable bug.

speaker: RATIFIED_DOC
subject: FK integrity
claim: PRAGMA foreign_keys is ON at session start and PRAGMA foreign_key_check returns empty on a healthy DB.

speaker: RATIFIED_DOC
subject: FK toggling in bulk-load migrations
claim: A bulk-load migration may toggle FK enforcement off within its script and back on at exit but must leave the DB referentially consistent.

speaker: PROCESS_RULE
subject: session bootstrap
claim: Each session loads project context via a bootstrap block at the start of the PI that pulls files from GitHub, queries data/guidebook.db and prints a status summary.

speaker: PROCESS_RULE
subject: bootstrap failure handling
claim: Bootstrap halts on critical fetch failure and logs [GAP: <filename> - not present] on non-critical failure.

speaker: PROCESS_RULE
subject: bootstrap budgets
claim: Bootstrap runs in under 30 seconds and under 100 lines.

speaker: PROCESS_RULE
subject: bootstrap fetch method
claim: Bootstrap uses the gh CLI when available and falls back to curl with a PAT.

speaker: PROCESS_RULE
subject: conflict row 1
claim: When a preference says X and the PI is silent, the preference applies.

speaker: PROCESS_RULE
subject: conflict row 2
claim: When the PI explicitly overrides a preference with a named clause, the PI applies.

speaker: PROCESS_RULE
subject: conflict row 3
claim: When a PI rule and skill content conflict on procedure, the skill wins on mechanics and the PI wins on whether the skill runs.

speaker: PROCESS_RULE
subject: conflict row 4
claim: When a text rule and a CI workflow disagree on the same check, CI wins and the drift is recorded as [ASSUMPTION] in the next session record.

speaker: PROCESS_RULE
subject: conflict row 5
claim: When an audit script and a CI workflow check the same thing, CI is authoritative and the script remains for local debugging.

speaker: PROCESS_RULE
subject: conflict row 6
claim: When two skills overlap on the same trigger, record a [GAP] in skill-registry.md and disambiguate explicitly.

speaker: PROCESS_RULE
subject: conflict row 7
claim: When the architecture spec and PI conflict, architecture wins on architectural rules and PI wins on project specifics.

speaker: PROCESS_RULE
subject: conflict row 8
claim: When bootstrap exceeds 100 lines or 30 seconds, extract the SQLite/state-query block to a bootstrap-status skill and leave a thin caller in the PI.

speaker: PROCESS_RULE
subject: conflict row 9
claim: A PI-referenced skill file that does not exist is acceptable only if labeled placeholder; otherwise record a [GAP] and author the skill or remove the reference.

speaker: PROCESS_RULE
subject: classifying a PI feature
claim: A new PI feature is classified as preference-level, project-specific, procedural or architectural before it is placed.

speaker: PROCESS_RULE
subject: audit script with enforcement change
claim: If a new PI rule is enforcement level 2 or higher, its audit script is written as part of the change.

speaker: PROCESS_RULE
subject: DR for workplan-level change
claim: A workplan-level change requires a DR in decisions/ referenced from the PI.

speaker: PROCESS_RULE
subject: state content in PI
claim: State content such as counts, retraction banners and session commentary belongs in DRs, audit scripts or the DB and not in PI standing rules.

speaker: PROCESS_RULE
subject: shipping a blocking audit script
claim: A blocking audit script is wired in by adding a job to the appropriate CI workflow.

speaker: PROCESS_RULE
subject: audit script location
claim: A new audit script is placed at scripts/audit/<name>.py following the enforcement-spectrum style.

speaker: PROCESS_RULE
subject: DR file naming
claim: A new DR is filed at decisions/DR-YYYY-MM-DD-<slug>.md.

speaker: PROCESS_RULE
subject: PI bump for a DR that sharpens a rule
claim: A DR that sharpens or adds a standing rule is paired with a drafted PI bump in governance/project-instructions-v<next>.md queued via decisions/PI-update-needed.md.

speaker: PROCESS_RULE
subject: PI bump go-live
claim: A PI bump goes live only when the owner manually pastes it into claude.ai project settings.

speaker: PROCESS_RULE
subject: currency header for architecture documents
claim: An architecture/*.md document describing schema content carries a currency header from creation, Governs schema work YES or NO with a historical-record note.

speaker: RATIFIED_DOC
subject: authoritative schema source
claim: scripts/migrations/ plus PRAGMA user_version are the authoritative schema source; a prose schema description is normative only where it says so.

speaker: PROCESS_RULE
subject: retiring content
claim: Retired content moves to _archived/ rather than being deleted, with subdirectories mirroring the origin location.

speaker: PROCESS_RULE
subject: caller sweep after rename or removal
claim: Removing or renaming a structural element is not complete until a caller sweep is performed.

speaker: PROCESS_RULE
subject: caller sweep verification
claim: The verification pass searches non-archived locations for the old name and confirms zero orphan references remain.

speaker: PROCESS_RULE
subject: renames substitute in every caller
claim: A rename substitutes the new name in every caller.

speaker: PROCESS_RULE
subject: scope assumptions
claim: The architecture assumes a single primary author, a single deployment surface (claude.ai chat) and no concurrent contributors.

speaker: PROCESS_RULE
subject: out-of-scope mechanics
claim: Pre-commit hooks, multi-surface PI specialization and contributor-coordination mechanics are out of scope until the scope assumptions change.

speaker: PROCESS_RULE
subject: PI size budget audit
claim: When the PI exceeds its size budget, it is audited for state content that should move out; the budget is set in the PI itself.

speaker: PROCESS_RULE
subject: bootstrap-exempt operations
claim: Pure governance work on the PI, preferences or architecture, tooling questions not touching repo state, and workflow conversations not touching repo content may skip the bootstrap.

speaker: RATIFIED_DOC
subject: DR to register-decision relation
claim: A Decision Record typically records the reasoning behind one or more register decisions, and a register decision may exist without any DR.

speaker: RATIFIED_DOC
subject: sessions directory
claim: sessions/ holds per-session records and the sessions/LATEST pointer.

speaker: RATIFIED_DOC
subject: workplan directory
claim: workplan/ holds active workplans and workplan/_superseded/ holds retired plans.

speaker: OWNER_QUOTED
subject: T2 vs T3 ranking
claim: Tier 2 ranks above Tier 3 (owner directive, enshrined).

speaker: RATIFIED_DOC
subject: Size of the ladder
claim: The evidence ladder has six numbered tiers T1-T6 plus two parallel community-knowledge tracks Co-1 and Co-2.

speaker: RATIFIED_DOC
subject: Meaning of tier number
claim: Tier number encodes the kind of claim a source can anchor, not source quality.

speaker: RATIFIED_DOC
subject: T1
claim: T1 is primary research with intervention-level or biomechanical control on the parameter under design.

speaker: RATIFIED_DOC
subject: T1 evidence_type
claim: T1 typically carries evidence_type clinical, occasionally grey for unpublished primary research.

speaker: RATIFIED_DOC
subject: T1 anchoring scope
claim: T1 anchors best-practice claims that turn on physiological, behavioural or biomechanical mechanism.

speaker: RATIFIED_DOC
subject: Co-1
claim: Co-1 is disability-led lived-experience publications (DPOs, named disability-organisation outputs, CRPD Art 4.3 consultation outputs).

speaker: RATIFIED_DOC
subject: Co-1 evidence_type and anchoring scope
claim: Co-1 carries evidence_type co1 and anchors best-practice claims that turn on user-stated preference, dignity, autonomy or self-determined accommodation.

speaker: RATIFIED_DOC
subject: Co-1 vs T1 rank
claim: Co-1 ranks alongside T1 (co-primary) because primary-research and lived-experience evidence are non-substitutable on different claim types.

speaker: RATIFIED_DOC
subject: T2
claim: T2 is community-consensus synthesis with two streams: (a) systematic reviews/meta-analyses and (b) named-organisation evidence-based standards.

speaker: RATIFIED_DOC
subject: T2 evidence_type
claim: T2 typically carries evidence_type sr_meta or standard_eb, occasionally co2 for community-of-professional synthesis.

speaker: RATIFIED_DOC
subject: T2 anchoring scope
claim: T2 anchors best-practice claims that turn on synthesised evidence across primary studies or on professional-body/DPO position.

speaker: RATIFIED_DOC
subject: Co-2
claim: Co-2 is OT/professional-body clinical practice guidelines, with evidence_type co2.

speaker: RATIFIED_DOC
subject: Co-2 anchoring scope
claim: Co-2 anchors best-practice claims that turn on clinical-professional consensus on rehabilitation or ADL adaptation.

speaker: RATIFIED_DOC
subject: T3
claim: T3 is lower-control clinical primary research plus grey-literature primary research.

speaker: RATIFIED_DOC
subject: T3 evidence_type
claim: T3 carries evidence_type clinical (predominant), grey, occasionally standard_eb for specialised technical guidance.

speaker: RATIFIED_DOC
subject: T3 anchoring scope
claim: T3 is supporting evidence for best-practice claims and is rarely the sole basis.

speaker: RATIFIED_DOC
subject: T4
claim: T4 is international standards published by international bodies, legally significant within their adoption scope.

speaker: RATIFIED_DOC
subject: T4 evidence_type
claim: T4 carries evidence_type standard_eb (predominant).

speaker: RATIFIED_DOC
subject: T4 anchoring scope
claim: T4 supports code-baseline citations, and supports best-practice claims only if the standard itself rests on T1/T2 evidence.

speaker: RATIFIED_DOC
subject: T5
claim: T5 is national beyond-code frameworks: best-practice guidance from national bodies that is not legally enforced.

speaker: RATIFIED_DOC
subject: T5 evidence_type
claim: T5 carries evidence_type national_fw (predominant) or standard_eb.

speaker: RATIFIED_DOC
subject: T5 anchoring scope
claim: T5 supports code-baseline citations, and supports best-practice claims only if the framework rests on T1/T2 evidence.

speaker: RATIFIED_DOC
subject: T6
claim: T6 is legally enforceable national or sub-national accessibility code, with evidence_type code.

speaker: RATIFIED_DOC
subject: T6 anchoring scope (original)
claim: T6 supports code-baseline citations and establishes the regulatory floor.

speaker: OWNER_RELAYED
subject: T6 anchoring scope (Option A)
claim: T6 anchors a weak-band (circle) "best practice as currently known" claim, flagged code-derived.

speaker: RATIFIED_DOC
subject: sr_meta tier
claim: Systematic reviews and meta-analyses (sr_meta) sit at Tier 2 alongside named-organisation evidence-based standards.

speaker: RATIFIED_DOC
subject: SR vs primary clinical
claim: A systematic review (warrant-source) ranks above the primary clinical studies it weighed (input-sources): SR > primary clinical.

speaker: RATIFIED_DOC
subject: sr_meta reservation
claim: evidence_type sr_meta (T2) is reserved for systematic reviews and meta-analyses with a defined method (risk-of-bias appraisal and/or effect synthesis).

speaker: RATIFIED_DOC
subject: Scoping review tier
claim: A scoping review anchors at T3, not T2.

speaker: RATIFIED_DOC
subject: Conceptual/framework paper tier
claim: A peer-reviewed conceptual/framework paper is primary work at T3.

speaker: RATIFIED_DOC
subject: National standards and design guides tier
claim: National accessibility standards and professional-body design guides sit at T5 national_fw at the standard/guidance level.

speaker: RATIFIED_DOC
subject: T5 vs T6 split
claim: A specific provision of a national standard becomes T6 only when cited as a legally-enforceable adopted code floor.

speaker: RATIFIED_DOC
subject: Convergence of T4-T6 as evidence
claim: Convergence of multiple Tier 4-6 sources on a value must not be treated as best-practice evidence.

speaker: RATIFIED_DOC
subject: Labelling converged code value best practice
claim: A value must not be labelled preferred or best practice merely because it converges across T5/T6 jurisdictions.

speaker: RATIFIED_DOC
subject: Use of T4-T6 citations
claim: Tier 4-6 citations are valid for code-baseline claims and jurisdiction-tracking work.

speaker: RATIFIED_DOC
subject: Binary anchoring rule
claim: Best-practice claims require T1, Co-1, T2 or Co-2 evidence; T4-T6 do not by themselves anchor them.

speaker: RATIFIED_DOC
subject: T4-T6-only claim
claim: A T4-T6-only claim may be stated, rendered at partial/weak strength with an explicit honesty flag.

speaker: RATIFIED_DOC
subject: Code-currency check
claim: A citation of a T4-T6 source must confirm the cited edition is the current legally-in-force edition, not a superseded one (applies inline to any new T4-T6 citation).

speaker: RATIFIED_DOC
subject: Code-currency age thresholds
claim: The code-currency audit fires at T4 age 7 years and T5/T6 age 5 years.

speaker: RATIFIED_DOC
subject: Audit suppression 1
claim: The code-currency audit is suppressed for a row with code_currency_status VERIFIED-CURRENT or PERMANENT-FRAMEWORK verified within 365 days.

speaker: RATIFIED_DOC
subject: Audit suppression 2
claim: The code-currency audit is suppressed when a supersession_check row with outcome current_best, co1_addition_logged or refined_by exists within 365 days (any slug).

speaker: RATIFIED_DOC
subject: Audit suppression 3
claim: The code-currency audit is suppressed when pub_year is within the tier-specific freshness threshold.

speaker: RATIFIED_DOC
subject: code_currency_status vocabulary
claim: code_currency_status takes VERIFIED-CURRENT, PERMANENT-FRAMEWORK, SUPERSEDED-PENDING-REPLACEMENT or UNVERIFIED-CHECK-DEFERRED.

speaker: RATIFIED_DOC
subject: Marker for confirmed evidence
claim: Marker filled-circle denotes T1, T2, T3-clinical, Co-1 and Co-2 sources.

speaker: RATIFIED_DOC
subject: Marker for policy/standards basis
claim: Marker half-circle denotes T4 and T5 sources (policy or standards basis only).

speaker: RATIFIED_DOC
subject: Marker for grey/thin base
claim: Marker open-circle denotes T3-grey, [EXPERT CONSENSUS], [THIN BASE], [UNSUPPORTED] and T6 (code-floor).

speaker: RATIFIED_DOC
subject: Legacy SR-as-Tier-4 mapping
claim: Systematic review/meta-analysis was formerly mapped to Tier 4 in the guidebook-auditor skill.

speaker: OWNER_RELAYED
subject: Weighted-strength anchor model
claim: Every tier can anchor a best-practice claim; claim strength is weighted by the tier of its evidence.

speaker: OWNER_RELAYED
subject: Purpose of tiers
claim: Tiers exist to let a reader grade confidence behind a proposal, not to gate whether a proposal may be stated.

speaker: RATIFIED_DOC
subject: Strength bands
claim: There are three anchoring strength bands: full, partial, weak.

speaker: RATIFIED_DOC
subject: Full band
claim: The full band (filled circle) comprises T1, Co-1, T2, Co-2 and T3-clinical, which anchor outright.

speaker: RATIFIED_DOC
subject: Partial band
claim: The partial band (half-circle) comprises T4 and T5, which anchor and are rendered as current standards practice.

speaker: RATIFIED_DOC
subject: Partial band flag
claim: Partial-band anchoring must be flagged "standards basis, not primary evidence."

speaker: RATIFIED_DOC
subject: Weak band
claim: The weak band (open circle) comprises T3-grey, T6 (code-floor) and expert-consensus/thin base, which anchor only a floor/convergence claim.

speaker: RATIFIED_DOC
subject: Weak band flag
claim: Weak-band anchoring must be rendered with the flag "best available given current regulation/practice, NOT academically adjudicated."

speaker: RATIFIED_DOC
subject: Honesty rule in weak band
claim: Convergence-not-evidence is retained as the honesty rule within the weak band.

speaker: OWNER_RELAYED
subject: Option A: T4-T6-only determination
claim: A determination whose basis is T4-T6 only is rendered as weak-band "best practice as currently known".

speaker: OWNER_RELAYED
subject: Option A: flag and ceiling
claim: Such a determination must always be flagged weak/code-derived with the convergence-not-evidence caveat, never unflagged and never rendered above the weak band.

speaker: OWNER_RELAYED
subject: Option A: no suppression
claim: When no stronger evidence exists, a T4-T6-only claim is stated-and-flagged as weak-band best practice, not suppressed and not merely labelled "regulatory floor".

speaker: RATIFIED_DOC
subject: T4-T6-only claim relabelled best practice
claim: A T4-T6-only claim is never relabelled "best practice".

speaker: OWNER_RELAYED
subject: Band assignment at determination level
claim: A determination (cell) whose entire basis is T4-T6 takes the weak band even where T4/T5 sources are present.

speaker: OWNER_RELAYED
subject: Scope of partial band
claim: The partial band applies to individual T4/T5 citations within an otherwise-anchored cell and to source-level markers, not to whole T4-T6-only determinations.

speaker: RATIFIED_DOC
subject: SR tiering
claim: Systematic reviews and meta-analyses are T2 (sr_meta).

speaker: RATIFIED_DOC
subject: Scoping/narrative review tiering
claim: Scoping reviews and narrative/literature reviews are T3 with evidence_type clinical or grey, never sr_meta.

speaker: RATIFIED_DOC
subject: Scoping/narrative review band
claim: Scoping and narrative reviews are supporting evidence in the filled-circle band but are not a T2 synthesis anchor.

speaker: RATIFIED_DOC
subject: Rapid review tiering
claim: A rapid review is T2 only if a systematic search and appraisal were retained; otherwise T3 (default).

speaker: RATIFIED_DOC
subject: Practitioner/firm work placement
claim: Practitioner and firm design work is tiered by method, not by authorship.

speaker: RATIFIED_DOC
subject: Practitioner/firm work authority
claim: Practitioner and firm design work sits below Co-1 and Co-2 in authority.

speaker: RATIFIED_DOC
subject: Firm POE tiering
claim: A firm POE or measured study is primary evidence at its method tier (T1 or T3).

speaker: RATIFIED_DOC
subject: Firm framework tiering
claim: A firm framework/index that genuinely synthesises evidence is T2-adjacent; otherwise supporting (T3).

speaker: RATIFIED_DOC
subject: Firm white-paper tiering
claim: Firm guidance or white-paper without method is T3-grey (weak band).

speaker: RATIFIED_DOC
subject: Firm source descriptive claims
claim: A firm or architect source can anchor a descriptive/measured claim at its method strength.

speaker: RATIFIED_DOC
subject: Role-appropriate-authority gate
claim: A firm or architect source cannot on its own anchor a functional-need claim; that requires Co-1 or Co-2.

speaker: RATIFIED_DOC
subject: Designer assertion flag
claim: A functional-need claim asserted by a firm alone must be flagged "designer assertion, unadjudicated."

speaker: RATIFIED_DOC
subject: Practice (Co-3) encoding
claim: A dedicated practice (Co-3) encoding exists in the DR but its audit representation is deferred to the audit rework.

speaker: RATIFIED_DOC
subject: Precedence of cited sources
claim: Where this document and a cited source diverge, the cited source governs until a DR reconciles them.

speaker: RATIFIED_DOC
subject: New doctrine in this document
claim: New doctrine appears only in passages flagged [NEW - DR-gated], each separately ratifiable.

speaker: RATIFIED_DOC
subject: Status of non-flagged content
claim: Everything not flagged new is restatement with citation, and the source documents govern.

speaker: RATIFIED_DOC
subject: Canonical home of ladder
claim: The canonical home of the tier ladder and Co-1/Co-2 co-primacy is tier-system.md section 1 (and mission-and-epistemics.md).

speaker: RATIFIED_DOC
subject: Canonical home of best-practice vs convergence
claim: T4-6-only determinations anchor at weak strength, never unflagged; individual T4/T5 citations carry the half-circle marker; canonical home is tier-system.md section 3 + 8.

speaker: RATIFIED_DOC
subject: Canonical home of state machine
claim: The four-state determination machine canonically lives in evidence-methodology.md section 2.

speaker: RATIFIED_DOC
subject: Canonical home of cell identity
claim: Cell identity and determination storage canonically live in DR-2026-07-12-evidence-cell-state-schema-reconciliation and migration 026.

speaker: RATIFIED_DOC
subject: Canonical home of T3-alone threshold
claim: The T3-alone stated threshold canonically lives in DR-2026-07-12-tier3-stated-threshold.md.

speaker: RATIFIED_DOC
subject: One evidence hierarchy
claim: There is exactly one evidence hierarchy, described as seven tiers with two co-primary community-knowledge tracks.

speaker: RATIFIED_DOC
subject: Governing principle of tiers
claim: Tier reflects what kind of claim a source can anchor, not how good the source is.

speaker: RATIFIED_DOC
subject: T1
claim: T1 is primary research with intervention-level or biomechanical control; OT-prioritized, not OT-exclusive.

speaker: RATIFIED_DOC
subject: Co-1 co-primary with T1
claim: Co-1 (disability-led lived-experience evidence, CRPD Art 4.3) is co-primary with T1.

speaker: RATIFIED_DOC
subject: T1 and Co-1 anchoring scope
claim: T1 anchors mechanism claims; Co-1 anchors user-stated preference, dignity, autonomy and self-determined accommodation claims.

speaker: RATIFIED_DOC
subject: T2 streams and Co-2 co-primacy
claim: T2 has two streams (systematic reviews/meta-analyses; named-organisation evidence-based standards) and Co-2 (OT professional-body CPGs) is co-primary with T2.

speaker: RATIFIED_DOC
subject: T3
claim: T3 is lower-control primary clinical plus grey-literature primary research; supporting, rarely the sole basis.

speaker: RATIFIED_DOC
subject: Regulatory stratum
claim: T4-T6 form the regulatory stratum, valid for code-baseline claims and jurisdiction tracking.

speaker: OWNER_RELAYED
subject: T4-T6 anchoring strength
claim: T4-T6 anchor best-practice claims only at weak weighted strength.

speaker: OWNER_RELAYED
subject: Regulatory value as best practice when no anchoring evidence
claim: Where no anchoring-band evidence exists, the regulatory value is stated as best practice as currently known, given that nothing stronger says otherwise.

speaker: OWNER_RELAYED
subject: Flag on regulatory-stratum anchoring
claim: Regulatory-stratum best-practice anchoring is always flagged weak/code-derived, never unflagged, with the convergence-not-evidence caveat intact.

speaker: RATIFIED_DOC
subject: Ladder never re-ranks
claim: No design mode, audience or weighting profile may reorder the tiers; only conditioning and emphasis vary.

speaker: RATIFIED_DOC
subject: Universal Mode
claim: Universal Mode is universal design/code compliance - the floor, not an aspiration - population-agnostic with fixed values.

speaker: RATIFIED_DOC
subject: Population Mode
claim: Population Mode is population-informed inclusive design with ranges and the median as default.

speaker: RATIFIED_DOC
subject: Person Mode
claim: Person Mode is person-specific co-design in which OT co-design resolves the individual's own specific functional needs (circumstances, capabilities, impairments, comorbidities).

speaker: RATIFIED_DOC
subject: Population bounding Person Mode answer
claim: A related disability population may inform but must not bound a Person Mode answer, which may fall outside any population range.

speaker: RATIFIED_DOC
subject: Tier and mode orthogonality
claim: Evidence tier and design mode are orthogonal axes of coverage: both always consulted, neither determining the other.

speaker: RATIFIED_DOC
subject: Scale-conditioned orthogonality
claim: The ladder is consulted at every design scale but its adjudicating force is asymmetric across scales.

speaker: RATIFIED_DOC
subject: Asymmetry principle: Universal
claim: At Universal Mode the anchoring authority is the code.

speaker: RATIFIED_DOC
subject: Asymmetry principle: Population
claim: At Population Mode the anchoring authority is the aggregate evidence ladder.

speaker: RATIFIED_DOC
subject: Asymmetry principle: Person
claim: At Person Mode the anchoring authority is the person themselves; published evidence conditions the assessment process and never overrides the assessed answer.

speaker: RATIFIED_DOC
subject: Source-ranking at Universal Mode
claim: At Universal Mode source-ranking is used only to justify exceeding the floor.

speaker: RATIFIED_DOC
subject: Parameter-value ladder at Person Mode
claim: The parameter-value ladder must not re-run at Person Mode.

speaker: RATIFIED_DOC
subject: Population source overriding individual
claim: No population-level source, including population-grain Co-1, may override an individual's assessed position.

subject: Matrix: T1 clinical x Universal Mode
claim: T1 clinical: ADJACENT at Universal Mode: supports raising the floor.

subject: Matrix: T1 clinical x Population Mode
claim: T1 clinical: Anchors at Population Mode (DIRECT; DOWN-WEIGHTED if it generalizes beyond what it measured).

speaker: RATIFIED_DOC
subject: Matrix: T1 clinical x Person Mode
claim: T1 clinical: Conditions the assessment process at Person Mode (DIRECT as grain).

subject: Matrix: Co-1 individual-grain x Universal Mode
claim: Co-1 individual-grain: ADJACENT at Universal Mode: supports raising the floor.

speaker: RATIFIED_DOC
subject: Matrix: Co-1 individual-grain x Population Mode
claim: Co-1 individual-grain: Anchors preference/dignity/autonomy claims at Population Mode (DIRECT unless generalizing beyond source).

speaker: RATIFIED_DOC
subject: Matrix: Co-1 individual-grain x Person Mode
claim: Co-1 individual-grain: At Person Mode honored as evidence but never substitutes for the person's own voice.

speaker: RATIFIED_DOC
subject: Matrix: Co-1 population-grain x Universal Mode
claim: Co-1 population-grain: ADJACENT at Universal Mode: supports raising the floor.

speaker: RATIFIED_DOC
subject: Matrix: Co-1 population-grain x Population Mode
claim: Co-1 population-grain: Anchors community-consensus claims at Population Mode (DIRECT).

subject: Matrix: Co-1 population-grain x Person Mode
claim: Co-1 population-grain: At Person Mode conditions but does not resolve (DOWN-WEIGHTED); population Co-1 does not override individual assessment.

subject: Matrix: T2 sr_meta x Universal Mode
claim: T2 sr_meta: ADJACENT at Universal Mode: supports raising the floor.

speaker: RATIFIED_DOC
subject: Matrix: T2 sr_meta x Population Mode
claim: T2 sr_meta: Anchors at Population Mode (DIRECT).

speaker: RATIFIED_DOC
subject: Matrix: T2 sr_meta x Person Mode
claim: T2 sr_meta: At Person Mode conditions but does not resolve (DOWN-WEIGHTED).

claim: T2 standard_eb: ADJACENT at Universal Mode: supports raising the floor.

subject: Matrix: T2 standard_eb x Population Mode
claim: T2 standard_eb: Anchors at Population Mode (DIRECT).

speaker: RATIFIED_DOC
subject: Matrix: T2 standard_eb x Person Mode
claim: T2 standard_eb: At Person Mode conditions but does not resolve (DOWN-WEIGHTED).

subject: Matrix: Co-2 OT CPGs x Universal Mode
claim: Co-2 OT CPGs: ADJACENT at Universal Mode: supports raising the floor.

speaker: RATIFIED_DOC
subject: Matrix: Co-2 OT CPGs x Population Mode
claim: Co-2 OT CPGs: Anchors at Population Mode (DIRECT).

subject: Matrix: Co-2 OT CPGs x Person Mode
claim: Co-2 OT CPGs: At Person Mode governs the assessment process (DOWN-WEIGHTED as parameter-value evidence; primary as process evidence).

subject: Matrix: T3 clinical/grey x Universal Mode
claim: T3 clinical/grey: ADJACENT at Universal Mode: supports.

subject: Matrix: T3 clinical/grey x Population Mode
claim: T3 clinical/grey: At Population Mode supports; anchors alone only per the tier3-threshold DR.

speaker: RATIFIED_DOC
subject: Matrix: T3 clinical/grey x Person Mode
claim: T3 clinical/grey: At Person Mode conditions assessment (DIRECT as grain).

subject: Matrix: T4-T5 standards/frameworks x Universal Mode
claim: T4-T5 standards/frameworks: Direct at Universal Mode: defines/raises the harmonised floor.

subject: Matrix: T4-T5 standards/frameworks x Population Mode
claim: T4-T5 standards/frameworks: At Population Mode grain-directness is NON-ANCHORING unless re-grained per G1; renders as weak-band best practice only when no anchoring evidence exists.

speaker: RATIFIED_DOC
subject: Matrix: T4-T5 standards/frameworks x Person Mode
claim: T4-T5 standards/frameworks: At Person Mode NON-ANCHORING.

subject: Matrix: T6 statutory code x Universal Mode
claim: T6 statutory code: Direct at Universal Mode: is the floor.

speaker: RATIFIED_DOC
subject: Matrix: T6 statutory code x Population Mode
claim: T6 statutory code: At Population Mode grain-directness is NON-ANCHORING; renders as weak-band best practice only when no anchoring evidence exists.

subject: Matrix: T6 statutory code x Person Mode
claim: T6 statutory code: At Person Mode NON-ANCHORING.

speaker: OWNER_RELAYED
subject: NON-ANCHORING meaning
claim: NON-ANCHORING is the mechanical grain-directness outcome: code-grain evidence cannot directly support a population-specific value.

speaker: OWNER_RELAYED
subject: Option A and directness layer
claim: Option A does not change the grain-directness outcomes in schemas/directness.py; it is a render/state-layer decision.

speaker: RATIFIED_DOC
subject: Re-grain of directness.py
claim: Any re-grain of schemas/directness.py must be a separately reviewed follow-up.

speaker: OWNER_RELAYED
subject: Render-anchoring at weak strength
claim: A determination whose entire basis is the regulatory stratum renders as a weak-band code-derived best-practice determination, always flagged and carrying the convergence-not-evidence caveat.

speaker: RATIFIED_DOC
subject: Person Mode and code value
claim: No code value anchors or resolves a Person Mode answer in either the directness or render sense.

speaker: OWNER_RELAYED
subject: Band assignment for regulatory_stratum_only
claim: Any regulatory_stratum_only cell renders at the weak band even where T4/T5 sources are present.

speaker: RATIFIED_DOC
subject: Directness not a hierarchy
claim: Directness is a categorical layer over the single ladder and must never become a separate hierarchy per scale.

speaker: RATIFIED_DOC
subject: Directness not numeric
claim: Directness conditioning must never be a numeric confidence score.

speaker: RATIFIED_DOC
subject: Directness dimensions
claim: Directness has three dimensions: population-directness (EXACT/PARTIAL/PROXY/MISMATCH), value-directness (EXACT/WITHIN-TOLERANCE/NOT-FOUND/CONTRADICTED), scale-directness (DIRECT/ADJACENT/DOWN-WEIGHTED/NON-ANCHORING).

speaker: RATIFIED_DOC
subject: Consolidated conditioning grade
claim: The three directness dimensions consolidate to one conditioning grade: DIRECT, DOWN-WEIGHTED, DISCOUNTED or NON-ANCHORING.

speaker: RATIFIED_DOC
subject: Grain-matching principle
claim: Directness is grain-matching, not specificity-ranking, and is bidirectional.

speaker: RATIFIED_DOC
subject: G1 re-graining rule
claim: A T4/T5 source is GRAIN_AGGREGATE only when its evidence basis is documented as traceable to T1/T2 evidence with provenance recorded on the source record; otherwise it keeps GRAIN_CODE.

speaker: RATIFIED_DOC
subject: Untraceable standards convergence
claim: Untraceable standards convergence stays in the regulatory stratum.

speaker: RATIFIED_DOC
subject: G2 NOT_ASSESSED vs not-applicable
claim: The directness engine distinguishes NOT_ASSESSED (dimension applies, no assessment) from not-applicable (dimension inapplicable).

speaker: RATIFIED_DOC
subject: NOT_ASSESSED cap
claim: A NOT_ASSESSED dimension caps consolidation at DOWN-WEIGHTED and flags the source for assessment.

speaker: RATIFIED_DOC
subject: Absence of assessment as directness
claim: Absence of assessment must never be treated as evidence of directness.

speaker: RATIFIED_DOC
subject: G3 Co-1 grain: DPO/advocacy
claim: Co-1 sources of co1_source_type dpo_research or advocacy_position are population-grain (GRAIN_AGGREGATE).

speaker: RATIFIED_DOC
subject: G3 Co-1 grain: narrative
claim: Co-1 sources of co1_source_type academic_narrative and individual-testimony corpora are individual-grain (GRAIN_SPECIFIC).

speaker: RATIFIED_DOC
subject: G3 Co-1 grain: literature/tool
claim: Co-1 sources of co1_source_type peer_reviewed_literature or validated_tool take grain per the study's own design, recorded per source.

speaker: RATIFIED_DOC
subject: DPO position paper at Person Mode
claim: A DPO position paper anchors Population-Mode claims and must not override an individual at Person Mode.

speaker: RATIFIED_DOC
subject: G6 grain by type x tier
claim: standard_eb at T2 has GRAIN_AGGREGATE; standard_eb at T4/T5 has GRAIN_CODE unless re-grained per G1.

speaker: RATIFIED_DOC
subject: G6 grain function
claim: Grain is derived from the (evidence_type, tier) pair, not from evidence_type alone.

speaker: RATIFIED_DOC
subject: Genealogy doctrine
claim: Precedent counts documents; evidence counts roots - agreement among many jurisdictions on one figure is one fact about transmission.

speaker: RATIFIED_DOC
subject: root_type vocabulary
claim: source_value_extractions.root_type takes measurement_primary, participatory_finding, committee_assertion, derived_calculation or untraced.

speaker: RATIFIED_DOC
subject: v_value_independence
claim: v_value_independence counts DISTINCT independent roots per parameter, excluding committee_assertion.

speaker: RATIFIED_DOC
subject: v_value_independence grain
claim: v_value_independence groups by parameter_id alone; the lens belongs to the determination, not the root count.

speaker: RATIFIED_DOC
subject: Root registry
claim: A root_id must resolve to a root_ref_id in evidence_sources or to a registered external-root stub.

speaker: RATIFIED_DOC
subject: Untraced rows
claim: Untraced rows carry NULL root_id and are excluded from the independent-root count.

speaker: RATIFIED_DOC
subject: Root classification dispute
claim: The root-versus-echo judgment must be recordably disputable via root_classification_basis and contested.

speaker: RATIFIED_DOC
subject: Six adjudication tests
claim: There are six adjudication tests (Root, Independence, Paradigm-commensurability, Fit-population, Currency, Interest); four are encoded, two doctrinal.

speaker: RATIFIED_DOC
subject: Currency test duplication
claim: The Currency test must use evidence_sources.superseded_by_ref_id and existing supersession machinery rather than duplicating it.

speaker: RATIFIED_DOC
subject: Interest test
claim: The Interest test is recorded in root_classification_basis notes and is not a column until a vocabulary emerges.

speaker: RATIFIED_DOC
subject: Derivations not identities
claim: Cross-paradigm and cross-device-class applications are recorded as derivations, never identities.

speaker: RATIFIED_DOC
subject: Manual-to-power chair figure
claim: A figure a source declares manual-wheelchair-only must not silently become a power-chair figure.

speaker: RATIFIED_DOC
subject: Citing root-independence on empty data
claim: No determination may cite root-independence until source_value_extractions has rows; an empty view is not a finding of no independence.

speaker: RATIFIED_DOC
subject: Determination cell key
claim: A determination cell is keyed on parameter_id crossed with at least one of identity_code, icf_code, needs_code, medical_code.

speaker: RATIFIED_DOC
subject: Four determination states
claim: Each determination cell holds exactly one of four states: stated, provisional, pending, not_applicable.

speaker: RATIFIED_DOC
subject: Determination is a pure function
claim: A determination is written by a pure function: same evidence plus same rule_version yields the same state and derivation_sha.

speaker: RATIFIED_DOC
subject: governing_refs on stated/provisional
claim: No stated or provisional determination may exist without non-empty governing_refs.

speaker: RATIFIED_DOC
subject: pending/not_applicable rows
claim: pending and not_applicable rows carry a gap link or rationale instead of governing_refs.

speaker: RATIFIED_DOC
subject: Scale-tagging (G1b)
claim: Every determination is tagged with the design scale its claim speaks to, and the tag governs what it may be called in every rendering.

speaker: RATIFIED_DOC
subject: Population-Mode best-practice determination
claim: A determination anchored in T1/Co-1/T2/Co-2 (T3 per its threshold DR) is a Population-Mode best-practice determination, the only kind rendered at anchoring strength.

speaker: OWNER_RELAYED
subject: Best-practice phrase after Option A
claim: The phrase "best practice" is no longer exclusive to anchored determinations; the weak band extends the phrase, never the strength.

speaker: RATIFIED_DOC
subject: Universal-Mode regulatory determination
claim: A determination whose entire basis is T4-6 is a Universal-Mode regulatory determination flagged regulatory_stratum_only.

speaker: OWNER_RELAYED
subject: Regulatory determination is weak-band best practice
claim: A regulatory_stratum_only determination is a best-practice determination at the weak band: best available as currently known, given that nothing stronger says otherwise.

speaker: RATIFIED_DOC
subject: regulatory_stratum_only state
claim: A regulatory_stratum_only determination has state provisional and is never stated.

speaker: RATIFIED_DOC
subject: v_best_practice weak-band row
claim: v_best_practice includes regulatory_stratum_only determinations as a queryably distinct weak-band row carrying a strength_band column.

speaker: RATIFIED_DOC
subject: Provisional flag names absent dimensions
claim: The provisional confidence flag names the absent anchoring dimensions, with teeth at T4/T5, not just T6.

speaker: OWNER_RELAYED
subject: Most-accommodating floor selection
claim: Where jurisdictions' floors differ, a regulatory-stratum determination anchors on the most accommodating available value read per the parameter's accessibility direction (best-for-the-user, not largest-number).

speaker: OWNER_RELAYED
subject: Parameter direction recorded
claim: The parameter's accessibility direction is recorded with the determination.

speaker: OWNER_RELAYED
subject: Passed-over floors remain visible
claim: Passed-over floors remain visible as the jurisdiction spread.

speaker: OWNER_RELAYED
subject: Population-contested direction
claim: Where the accessibility direction is population-contested, most-accommodating selection is inapplicable: no single value is anchored, the conflict is recorded via the conflicts machinery, and the spread is rendered with each population's direction stated.

speaker: RATIFIED_DOC
subject: Accessibility-direction metadata
claim: Per-parameter accessibility direction lives in base_parameters.accessibility_direction, with rationale required by the schema and written by db.py set-parameter-direction.

speaker: RATIFIED_DOC
subject: value_note decline reason
claim: Where the engine cannot compose a value it records the reason in specifications.value_note.

speaker: RATIFIED_DOC
subject: Person Mode determinations
claim: Person Mode produces no stored determinations.

speaker: RATIFIED_DOC
subject: Person-Mode handoff
claim: For Person Mode the guidebook stores only the handoff: the functional parameter driving assessment and the population-range scaffold.

speaker: OWNER_RELAYED
subject: Mandatory flagging not suppression
claim: The anti-laundering closure works by mandatory flagging rather than suppression.

speaker: OWNER_RELAYED
subject: Regulatory value rendering ceiling
claim: A regulatory-stratum value must never be rendered unflagged, above the (provisional, regulatory_stratum_only) register-map row, or with the convergence-not-evidence caveat dropped.

speaker: OWNER_RELAYED
subject: Flag binds every rendering
claim: The flag-and-caveat requirement binds every rendering of a regulatory-stratum value, not only best-practice-phrased ones.

speaker: RATIFIED_DOC
subject: G7 stated threshold admits T2
claim: The stated threshold admits T2 anchors explicitly (both streams), keeping the G6 grain rule so T2-standard anchoring never leaks to T4/T5.

speaker: RATIFIED_DOC
subject: G8 pending_assessment rendering
claim: A pending_assessment cell may render only with the value-level-convergence-pending disclosure in every register.

speaker: RATIFIED_DOC
subject: Derivation handshake fields
claim: Every determination records functional_basis and derivation_paths, where derivation_paths is dual, population_only or function_only.

speaker: RATIFIED_DOC
subject: Dual-path convergence
claim: Dual-path convergence (population and function derivations) is recorded as itself evidence.

speaker: RATIFIED_DOC
subject: Single-path assertion
claim: A single-path derivation is permitted only with a named-path rationale.

speaker: OWNER_RELAYED
subject: Cultural claims as population_only
claim: Claims whose normative force is community-rooted remain fully assertable as population_only.

speaker: OWNER_RELAYED
subject: Bottom-up override of community claim
claim: No functional derivation may flatten, reduce or override a community claim; there is no bottom-up override of Co-1.

speaker: OWNER_RELAYED
subject: Cultural-claim protection scope
claim: The cultural/dignity-claim protection binds every register, every audience and the engine.

speaker: RATIFIED_DOC
subject: Community-rooted boundary criterion
claim: Community-rooted means anchored by Co-1/participatory provenance (dpo_research, advocacy_position, participatory peer-reviewed work) or an equivalent documented community process.

speaker: RATIFIED_DOC
subject: Cultural exemption by assertion
claim: A population_only claim without a community anchor owes the standard named-path rationale and gains no cultural exemption by assertion.

speaker: RATIFIED_DOC
subject: population_icf_links
claim: The population-to-function mapping is one table, population_icf_links: population code x ICF d-code x mechanism x confidence x provenance.

speaker: RATIFIED_DOC
subject: FDA crosswalk reconciliation
claim: The FDA-code to population-code crosswalk records every mapping as a row and logs every unmapped code as a finding, with no silent aliasing.

speaker: RATIFIED_DOC
subject: H4 handshake gate
claim: FDA verdicts UNLINKED/MISLINKED/UNDER-CONSERVATIVE and FDR delta-classification CONTRADICTS force the affected cell to provisional, never stated, until resolved.

speaker: RATIFIED_DOC
subject: Gate binds only where run
claim: The H4 gate binds only where a check has actually run.

speaker: RATIFIED_DOC
subject: Ladder-inversion guard
claim: Gate rows carry the tier and type of the triggering source so a grey-tier CONTRADICTS cannot indefinitely pin a T1-anchored cell.

speaker: RATIFIED_DOC
subject: Gate resolution path
claim: Gate resolution is by evidence-auditor adjudication recorded on the cell with its rationale.

speaker: RATIFIED_DOC
subject: Gate direction
claim: A binding handshake gate caps a cell at provisional and never moves it in any other direction.

speaker: RATIFIED_DOC
subject: Single-path determination without rationale or anchor
claim: The database refuses a single-path determination carrying neither a named-path rationale nor a cultural anchor.

speaker: RATIFIED_DOC
subject: Cultural anchor must anchor
claim: The cultural anchor must actually anchor: derivation_handshake_integrity reads the anchor's own co1_source_type through the G3 predicate.

speaker: RATIFIED_DOC
subject: Participatory peer-reviewed claims narrowing
claim: A claim anchored only by participatory peer-reviewed Co-1 work currently owes the standard named-path rationale instead of taking the cultural exemption.

speaker: RATIFIED_DOC
subject: Participatory flag
claim: When a participatory flag exists, the cultural-exemption predicate in assess_cell.derivation_handshake() is to be widened.

speaker: RATIFIED_DOC
subject: derivation_handshake_integrity blocking promotion
claim: Whether derivation_handshake_integrity is promoted to blocking is an owner call, deliberately not taken.

speaker: RATIFIED_DOC
subject: Audience structure
claim: Primary audiences are designers and disabled people; secondary audiences are occupational therapists and policymakers.

speaker: RATIFIED_DOC
subject: Role does not change data
claim: Role changes emphasis and register but must not change the underlying data.

speaker: RATIFIED_DOC
subject: Advocacy-brief use-pattern (G5)
claim: Advocacy is a use-pattern within the disabled-person primary audience, not a fifth audience.

subject: Claim-strength register map
claim: Every rendering of a determination must draw claim-strength language from a single map keyed by the determination tuple, with one language cell per register.

subject: Determination tuple
claim: The determination tuple is (state, tier_basis, convergence, conditioning summary, regulatory_stratum_only).

speaker: RATIFIED_DOC
subject: Weighting profile and register map
claim: Emphasis re-ranking by weighting_profile chooses which cells are foregrounded but can never move a rendering to a different row of the register map.

speaker: RATIFIED_DOC
subject: Policymaker register anti-laundering language
claim: The policymaker register carries the strongest anti-laundering language for provisional regulatory_stratum_only cells.

speaker: RATIFIED_DOC
subject: Register map row: provisional regulatory_stratum_only
claim: For (provisional, regulatory_stratum_only) the technical register reads "Best practice as currently known: X [weak, code-derived]" with the no-anchoring-evidence caveat.

speaker: RATIFIED_DOC
subject: Invariant I1
claim: Every rendering of a cell, in every register, carries the identical determination tuple.

speaker: RATIFIED_DOC
subject: Invariant I2: floor-anchor pairing
claim: A rendering showing a regulatory floor value alongside an evidence-anchored value must show both and label which is which.

speaker: RATIFIED_DOC
subject: Invariant I2: policymaker delta
claim: Where an evidence-anchored value exists, the policymaker register renders the delta, never the floor alone.

subject: Invariant I2: stratum-only cell
claim: On a regulatory_stratum_only cell the policymaker register renders the weak-band value under I3's mandatory flag and caveat with the jurisdiction spread visible.

speaker: OWNER_RELAYED
subject: Invariant I3
claim: Regulatory-stratum-only cells carry no unflagged and no above-weak-band best-practice language in any register under any weighting profile.

speaker: OWNER_RELAYED
subject: Invariant I3: flag, caveat, ceiling

speaker: RATIFIED_DOC
subject: Invariant I4
claim: Plain-language translations of the markers come only from the register map, not ad-hoc prose.

speaker: RATIFIED_DOC
subject: Invariant I5
claim: No register may express claim strength exceeding its register-map row.

subject: Invariant I5: brevity and flags

subject: Tier N reservation

subject: Carer as proxy

subject: Representation-checking

subject: Solo-authorship disclosure

subject: Limits rendered

speaker: RATIFIED_DOC

speaker: PROCESS_RULE
subject: Adversarial pair
claim: An adversarial pass runs a read-only critic (antagonist) and a separate writer that repairs.

speaker: PROCESS_RULE
subject: Self-checking
claim: One model must not check its own work in the adversarial pass.

speaker: PROCESS_RULE
subject: No agent-launching tool
claim: If no agent-launching tool is available, say so in the handback and stop.

speaker: PROCESS_RULE
subject: Self-administered pass
claim: The antagonist's checklist must not be run by the author and called a pass.

speaker: PROCESS_RULE
subject: Self-administered pass
claim: A self-administered pass is not a pass.

speaker: PROCESS_RULE
subject: record-adversarial-pass refusal
claim: db.py record-adversarial-pass refuses a pass whose reviewer and author transcripts are the same file.

speaker: PROCESS_RULE
subject: Capturing SUBJECT_COMMIT
claim: Before launching the critic, capture SUBJECT_COMMIT="$(git rev-parse HEAD)", the sha the reviewer will actually read.

speaker: PROCESS_RULE
subject: Capturing SUBJECT_COMMIT after repair
claim: SUBJECT_COMMIT must not be captured after step 2's repair, because that names the repaired state rather than what was reviewed.

speaker: PROCESS_RULE
subject: Launching the antagonist
claim: Launch the antagonist agent (Fable, read-only) against the stated target.

speaker: PROCESS_RULE
subject: Critic summarising work
claim: The critic attacks the claim and does not summarize the work.

speaker: PROCESS_RULE
subject: Critic proposing repair
claim: The critic does not propose the repair.

speaker: PROCESS_RULE
subject: Finding content
claim: Every critic finding names the artifact and line and states the failure case.

speaker: PROCESS_RULE
subject: Gate-should-have-caught check
claim: A finding that a gate should have caught is checked against whether that gate had a SUBJECT.

speaker: PROCESS_RULE
subject: Critic counts
claim: Every count the critic cites is one it just computed.

speaker: PROCESS_RULE
subject: NULL marker
claim: Where the critic found nothing, it states [NULL: <scope> — examined, nothing found] rather than silence.

speaker: PROCESS_RULE
subject: Adjudicate before repair
claim: Findings are adjudicated first, then repaired.

speaker: PROCESS_RULE
subject: Per-finding confirmation
claim: For each finding, confirm it against the artifact yourself, then fix it or reject it with a reason.

speaker: PROCESS_RULE
subject: Irreproducible finding
claim: A finding that cannot be reproduced is not a finding; say so and move on.

speaker: PROCESS_RULE
subject: Recording after transcript commit
claim: The pass is recorded only once the critic's transcript is committed (rule 6) and carries the closing adversarial-findings JSON block.

speaker: PROCESS_RULE
subject: Scratch DB for recording
claim: Recording the pass is done on a scratch copy of the DB.

speaker: PROCESS_RULE
subject: db.py refusal on canonical DB
claim: record-adversarial-pass, like every db.py subcommand, refuses to open the canonical DB read-write.

speaker: PROCESS_RULE
subject: Recording the adversarial pass
claim: Record the pass with db.py record-adversarial-pass using --subject-session, --subject-commit, --reviewer-transcript, --author-transcript and --session.

speaker: PROCESS_RULE
subject: Write path for adversarial-pass row
claim: The adversarial-pass row travels the ordinary write path (emit_batch_sql, emit_data_migration, migrate_db) with the batch's rows.

speaker: PROCESS_RULE
subject: Classification of adversarial-pass row
claim: The adversarial-pass row is research data (RC6), not tooling.

speaker: PROCESS_RULE
subject: Shipping adversarial-pass row
claim: The adversarial-pass row ships in the batch's data migration.

speaker: PROCESS_RULE
subject: Hand-applying adversarial-pass row
claim: The adversarial-pass row is never hand-applied to the canonical DB.

speaker: PROCESS_RULE
subject: Disposing each finding
claim: Each finding is disposed with db.py dispose-adversarial-finding.

speaker: PROCESS_RULE
subject: Disposition vocabulary
claim: Finding disposition takes one of four values: REPAIRED, REJECTED, PROVISIONAL-DISPUTED, OWNER-RULED.

speaker: PROCESS_RULE
subject: REPAIRED disposition content
claim: A REPAIRED disposition names the data migration path that fixed the finding.

speaker: PROCESS_RULE
subject: OWNER-RULED disposition content
claim: An OWNER-RULED disposition names the exact ledger quote, which must occur once.

speaker: PROCESS_RULE
subject: Closing the pass last
claim: After recording and disposing, close the pass with db.py close-adversarial-pass --pass-id N --session ....

speaker: PROCESS_RULE
subject: close-adversarial-pass refusal condition
claim: close-adversarial-pass refuses until every lens is covered and at least one row is SURVIVED.

speaker: OWNER_RELAYED
subject: Closing adversarial pass 1
claim: close-adversarial-pass must never be run on pass 1; the owner ruling of 2026-09-27 (second) holds pass 1 open.
enforcement: NOT ENFORCED (text: 'Nothing refuses either; you are the gate.')

speaker: PROCESS_RULE
subject: Closing adversarial pass 2
claim: Pass 2 stays open per the process-gap plan approved 2026-10-01, so close-adversarial-pass must not be run on it.
enforcement: NOT ENFORCED (text: 'Nothing refuses either; you are the gate.')

speaker: PROCESS_RULE
subject: Finding admitted only on the database file
claim: A finding admitted only on the database file is closed but printed as REPORTED, because the database is not an artefact of attack.

speaker: PROCESS_RULE
subject: Gate before claiming done
claim: Before claiming done, run scripts/preflight.sh and python3 scripts/run_checks.py --selftest.

speaker: PROCESS_RULE
subject: Selftest after any rename
claim: run_checks.py --selftest is mandatory after any rename.

speaker: PROCESS_RULE
subject: Adversarial report content
claim: Report the findings and their disposition.

speaker: PROCESS_RULE
subject: Critique as deliverable
claim: The critique is not the deliverable; the repair is.

speaker: PROCESS_RULE
subject: Self-declared batch completion
claim: A research batch must never be claimed done from one's own reading of it.

speaker: PROCESS_RULE
subject: Running the batch-done gate
claim: Run the gate the SessionStart contract names (three audit scripts) to decide whether a batch is finished.

speaker: PROCESS_RULE
subject: research_batch_dod on CURRENT
claim: Run scripts/audit/research_batch_dod.py with --session set to the contents of scratchpad/CURRENT.

speaker: PROCESS_RULE
subject: adversarial_pass_audit on CURRENT
claim: Run scripts/audit/adversarial_pass_audit.py with --session set to the contents of scratchpad/CURRENT.

speaker: PROCESS_RULE
subject: search_log_completeness on CURRENT
claim: Run scripts/audit/search_log_completeness.py with --session set to the contents of scratchpad/CURRENT.

speaker: PROCESS_RULE
subject: RC4 failure condition
claim: adversarial_pass_audit fails if the session wrote to any of the 2026-08-19 RULE's research tables and no closed adversarial pass names it.

speaker: PROCESS_RULE
subject: Scope of the RC4 audit
claim: Run the RC4 audit on CURRENT.

speaker: PROCESS_RULE
subject: RC4 via research battery
claim: Do not run the RC4 audit via run_checks.py --battery research.

speaker: PROCESS_RULE
subject: I5 failure condition
claim: search_log_completeness (I5) fails a WebSearch query that no search_executions.query_text of the session contains, i.e. a search run and not logged (R8).

speaker: PROCESS_RULE
subject: Backfilling an unlogged search
claim: A WebSearch that was run but not logged is logged with db.py log-search --backfill 1.

speaker: PROCESS_RULE
subject: Post hoc marking of backfilled search
claim: The --prior-expectation on a backfilled log-search row is written after the results, so it is post hoc and must say so.

speaker: PROCESS_RULE
subject: REPORTED lines of I5
claim: I5's REPORTED lines (unpersisted WebFetch URLs, bare curl/wget hosts, web rows with no ledger line) belong in the session record; they do not fail and a NOTHING-IN-SCOPE verdict does not clear them.

speaker: PROCESS_RULE
subject: Coverage limit of I5
claim: I5 witnesses WebSearch and WebFetch only; a search run through an MCP tool (Consensus, PubMed, Scholar Gateway) leaves no ledger line, so a PASS says nothing about those.

speaker: PROCESS_RULE
subject: Session id form
claim: The session id is the bare stem in the DB and carries .md in pointer files; the wrong form scopes the gate to zero rows.

speaker: PROCESS_RULE
subject: Batch-done failure
claim: If the batch-done gate fails, the batch is not done.

speaker: PROCESS_RULE
subject: Response to batch-done failure
claim: On failure, fix the rows, re-emit and re-run the gate.

speaker: PROCESS_RULE
subject: Baselining a batch-done failure
claim: A batch-done failure must not be baselined away.

speaker: PROCESS_RULE
subject: Research contract baseline direction
claim: governance/research-contract-baseline.json ratchets down only; raising a count there forgives fresh violations invisibly.

speaker: PROCESS_RULE
subject: Corpus regression check
claim: When the gate passes, run python3 scripts/audit/research_batch_dod.py --all to confirm the corpus posture has not regressed.

speaker: PROCESS_RULE
subject: Committing scratchpad and transcripts last
claim: After the gate passes and the regression check, commit the scratchpad and agent transcripts via scripts/preserve_transcripts.py.

speaker: PROCESS_RULE
subject: Orientation first
claim: Orient from live state before doing anything else.

speaker: PROCESS_RULE
subject: Derive figures
claim: Every figure is derived from live state and never quoted from a document, including this file (CLAUDE.md rule 7a).

speaker: PROCESS_RULE
subject: ensure-deps
claim: Run bash .claude/hooks/ensure-deps.sh when orienting.

speaker: PROCESS_RULE
subject: Read CURRENT
claim: Read scratchpad/CURRENT to learn the session running now.

speaker: PROCESS_RULE
subject: List checks
claim: Run python3 scripts/run_checks.py --list to see the registry and quarantine.

speaker: PROCESS_RULE
subject: Use db-census
claim: Establish live DB state with the db-census agent (Haiku).

speaker: PROCESS_RULE
subject: Opus for counts
claim: Opus-class models are not spent on counts.

speaker: PROCESS_RULE
subject: Census: row counts and empties
claim: Orientation establishes row counts per table and which tables are empty.

speaker: PROCESS_RULE
subject: Census: unwritable tables
claim: Orientation establishes which tables are unwritable through a NOT NULL FK into an emptied table.

speaker: PROCESS_RULE
subject: Census: schema version
claim: Orientation establishes PRAGMA user_version.

speaker: PROCESS_RULE
subject: Orientation reading order
claim: Read first decisions/DR-2026-08-19-research-restart-operative-instrument.md, then the tail of references/project-standards.md.

speaker: PROCESS_RULE
subject: Orientation reading set
claim: Orientation reads only two documents: the 2026-08-19 operative-instrument DR and the tail of references/project-standards.md.

speaker: PROCESS_RULE
subject: Latest owner rulings supersede
claim: The latest owner rulings at the tail of references/project-standards.md supersede every ratified record they touch on contact (rule 0).

speaker: PROCESS_RULE
subject: Search tool for hidden paths
claim: Because .ignore hides sessions/, _archived/, audits/ and versions/ from ripgrep and the Grep tool, use grep -r or git grep.

speaker: PROCESS_RULE
subject: Reporting a ruling absent
claim: Never report a ruling absent from a search that could not have seen it.

speaker: PROCESS_RULE
subject: LATEST pointers
claim: sessions/LATEST and LATEST-RESEARCH move at CLOSE, so both name the previous session for the whole life of the current one.

speaker: PROCESS_RULE
subject: Orientation report
claim: The orientation report states the pipeline state, the live blockers and the single next action.

speaker: PROCESS_RULE
subject: Assumptions in orientation
claim: Assumptions are stated inline in the orientation report.

speaker: PROCESS_RULE
subject: Plan document at orientation
claim: Do not produce a plan document at orientation unless asked.

speaker: PROCESS_RULE
subject: Opening a session first
claim: Run the session-open steps first, before any other work.

speaker: PROCESS_RULE
subject: When CURRENT moves
claim: scratchpad/CURRENT moves at session OPEN.

speaker: PROCESS_RULE
subject: PostToolUse command log routing
claim: The PostToolUse hook writes every Bash, WebSearch and WebFetch call to whatever scratchpad/CURRENT names.

speaker: PROCESS_RULE
subject: CURRENT content form
claim: scratchpad/CURRENT holds the DB session stem (session_YYYY-MM-DD-<slug>), not a bare branch slug.

speaker: PROCESS_RULE
subject: Scratchpad folder name equals CURRENT content
claim: The scratchpad folder name and scratchpad/CURRENT's content must be identical.

speaker: PROCESS_RULE
subject: record-command.py CURRENT handling
claim: .claude/hooks/record-command.py only honours CURRENT when scratchpad/<CURRENT's content> is a real directory; otherwise it falls back to a same-harness-sid guess.

speaker: PROCESS_RULE
subject: Creating the scratchpad folder as the stem
claim: Create the scratchpad folder named exactly as the session stem from the start, never as a bare slug.

speaker: PROCESS_RULE
subject: Default slug
claim: The slug defaults to the argument or, absent one, the current branch name with any prefix before the last slash removed.

speaker: PROCESS_RULE
subject: Session stem form
claim: The session stem is session_<UTC date YYYY-MM-DD>-<slug>.

speaker: PROCESS_RULE
subject: Creating the stem folder
claim: Create the directory scratchpad/<stem> when opening a session.

speaker: PROCESS_RULE
subject: Writing CURRENT
claim: Write the stem into scratchpad/CURRENT after creating the folder.

speaker: PROCESS_RULE
subject: Renaming the folder once PR exists
claim: Rename the scratchpad folder with git mv once the PR number exists.

speaker: PROCESS_RULE
subject: Renaming CURRENT to match folder
claim: Leave scratchpad/CURRENT's content as the DB stem when the folder is renamed; do not rename it to match.

speaker: PROCESS_RULE
subject: Routing of renamed folder
claim: A folder rename that keeps a session_ or pr- prefix stays routed correctly through the hook's fallback with no direct-match window.

speaker: PROCESS_RULE
subject: CURRENT value that matches no folder
claim: scratchpad/CURRENT must not be changed to a value that names neither the current folder nor any session_- or pr--prefixed folder that exists.

speaker: PROCESS_RULE
subject: Matching folder when changing CURRENT
claim: When changing CURRENT, create or rename the matching folder in the same action.

speaker: PROCESS_RULE
subject: Recording session kind
claim: State in the first status update whether the session is a research session or a tooling session (RC6).

speaker: PROCESS_RULE
subject: Research session
claim: A research session writes rows only: evidence, judgment and synthesis.

speaker: PROCESS_RULE
subject: Tooling session
claim: A tooling session covers schema, scripts, checks and governance prose and writes no research rows.

speaker: PROCESS_RULE
subject: Mixed research/tooling changeset
claim: A single session's changeset must not contain both research-data paths and tooling paths.

speaker: PROCESS_RULE
subject: Handling a mid-batch writer gap
claim: A session that finds it needs both kinds mid-way files the writer gap as a GAP and either leaves the rows unwritten or writes them through existing CLI verbs.

speaker: PROCESS_RULE
subject: Tooling PR before batch
claim: The tooling fix ships in its own PR merged to main first, and the batch branch takes it with git merge origin/main.

speaker: PROCESS_RULE
subject: Confirming previous session closed
claim: After opening, confirm the previous session closed cleanly with python3 scripts/preserve_transcripts.py --check.

speaker: PROCESS_RULE
subject: preserve_transcripts --check state
claim: preserve_transcripts.py --check is red for the whole life of a live session by construction.

speaker: PROCESS_RULE
subject: Using --check as gate
claim: --check output is read for what is unpreserved from before this session, not as a gate on the current one.

speaker: PROCESS_RULE
subject: When the antagonist is used
claim: The antagonist is used after any substantive piece of work (research batch, migration, reasoning document, diff) to attack the claim before it is ratified.

speaker: PROCESS_RULE
subject: Antagonist writing or repairing
claim: The antagonist is not used to write, fix or plan the repair.

speaker: PROCESS_RULE
subject: Antagonist tool set
claim: The antagonist's tools are Read, Grep, Glob and Bash (no write tool).

speaker: PROCESS_RULE
subject: Antagonist model
claim: The antagonist runs on the fable model.

speaker: PROCESS_RULE
subject: Antagonist role
claim: The antagonist attacks the claim.

speaker: PROCESS_RULE
subject: Antagonist proposing repairs
claim: The antagonist does not propose repairs.

speaker: PROCESS_RULE
subject: Antagonist attack order
claim: The antagonist looks for five things in order: a gate that examined nothing; a number that could be wrong tomorrow; an unsupported claim; an already-made ruling; a fabricated or unverified bibliographic field.

speaker: PROCESS_RULE
subject: Look for vacuous gates
claim: The antagonist looks for a gate that passed having examined nothing.

speaker: PROCESS_RULE
subject: Check subject
claim: For every check cited as evidence, ask what its SUBJECT was.

speaker: PROCESS_RULE
subject: EXAMINED 0 under PASS
claim: EXAMINED: 0 under a PASS is not a pass.

speaker: PROCESS_RULE
subject: Wrong-form session id
claim: A session id in the wrong form (.md where the DB holds a bare stem) scopes a gate to zero rows and reports green.

speaker: PROCESS_RULE
subject: Look for stale numbers
claim: The antagonist looks for a number that could be wrong tomorrow with nothing going red (literals, thresholds, min_items, lists, globs, prose restating a checked value).

speaker: PROCESS_RULE
subject: Recompute figures
claim: The antagonist recomputes every figure it is asked to accept.

speaker: PROCESS_RULE
subject: Prose callers unswept
claim: Prose callers are swept by no gate at all.

speaker: PROCESS_RULE
subject: Look for unsupported claims
claim: The antagonist looks for a claim the artifact does not support.

speaker: PROCESS_RULE
subject: Read the artifact
claim: Read the artifact, not the summary of it.

speaker: PROCESS_RULE
subject: 0-row object
claim: A 0-row object is unproven, not clean.

speaker: PROCESS_RULE
subject: Look for already-made rulings
claim: The antagonist looks for a ruling that was already made, since owner rulings supersede ratified records on contact.

speaker: PROCESS_RULE
subject: Search tool for rulings
claim: Search for rulings with grep -r or git grep, because .ignore hides sessions/ from ripgrep and the Grep tool.

speaker: PROCESS_RULE
subject: Reporting a ruling absent
claim: Never report a ruling absent from a search that could not have seen it.

speaker: PROCESS_RULE
subject: Look for fabricated bibliographic fields
claim: The antagonist looks for a fabricated or unverified bibliographic field.

speaker: PROCESS_RULE
subject: Diff stored data against payload
claim: Diff stored bibliographic data against the persisted payload in retrieval-log/.

speaker: PROCESS_RULE
subject: Antagonist DB access mode
claim: The antagonist opens the database read-only via sqlite3.connect('file:data/guidebook.db?mode=ro', uri=True).

speaker: PROCESS_RULE
subject: Antagonist refuses writes
claim: If asked to write, the antagonist refuses and says why.

speaker: PROCESS_RULE
subject: Antagonist finding shape
claim: Each finding is one block giving the artifact and line, the claim, the failure case that breaks it and the command that shows it.

speaker: PROCESS_RULE
subject: Antagonist finding order
claim: Findings are ranked worst first.

speaker: PROCESS_RULE
subject: No false balance
claim: No false balance: report every broken thing found.

speaker: PROCESS_RULE
subject: NULL marker (antagonist)
claim: Where nothing was found, say [NULL: <scope examined> — examined, nothing found].

speaker: PROCESS_RULE
subject: Softening findings
claim: The antagonist does not soften findings.

speaker: PROCESS_RULE
subject: Summarising work back
claim: The antagonist does not summarize the work back.

speaker: PROCESS_RULE
subject: Overall verdict
claim: The antagonist does not close with a verdict on whether the work is good overall.

speaker: PROCESS_RULE
subject: Lens coverage in closing block
claim: Each of the eleven lenses must appear at least once in the closing block before the pass can be closed.
enforcement: db.py close-adversarial-pass refuses until every lens is covered

speaker: PROCESS_RULE
subject: Lens L1-existence
claim: Adversarial lens L1-existence tests: The source/row/artefact cited actually resolves — it exists.
